newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in late rebound on speculative buys.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in late rebound on speculative buys.

text.p: Mexican staged a late recovery Wednesday after sliding for most of the day to close slightly higher.
Traders said the bourse rebounded on bargain hunting in some stocks as dealers believed prices had touched bottom after falling sharply on Monday and Tuesday.
"Late buying in Cemex and Kimber bolstered the IPC as they are blue chips. It didn't take much volume to turn the bourse around," a Mexico City floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 1.92 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,716.18. Volume was quiet at just 42.8 million shares.
Cement makers Cemex CPO shares gained 50 centavos (6 cents) to 28.70 pesos ($3.62). Paper company Kimber ended up 75 centavos (9 cents) at 32.10 pesos ($4.05).
The three stocks together accounted for 7.5 percent of all shares traded.
Sears de Mexico topped the gainers' list following news Mexican holding company Grupo Carso will buy a 60 percent stake in the retailer from parent company Sears, Roebuck Co.
Sears B1 shares soared 2.64 pesos (33 cents), or 18 percent, to 17.54 pesos ($2.21), after gainly strongly on Monday and Tuesday amid rumours the Carso deal was about to be settled.
Grupo Carso meanwhile gained 35 centavos (4 cents) to 45.15 pesos ($5.70).
